[MUJAHID:v1p386#3/r1] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | holds | Mujahid glosses the command to leave Abraham alone for maliyyan as for a time.
[MUQATIL:19:45-48/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Azar asks whether Ibrahim rejects his idols and threatens to stone him, meaning insult him here; elsewhere in the Qur'an the same threat means killing.
[MUQATIL:19:45-48/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Maliyyan means for the length of Azar's life or, alternatively, for a long time: Ibrahim must leave and prolong the separation.
[MUQATIL:19:45-48/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains Azar's instruction as leaving him unharmed, without suffering injury from him.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With a demonstrative, the following noun is the predicate and an accusative descriptor is a circumstantial state, as in هذا عبد الله منطلقا.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | This construction draws attention to someone in a state such as departing; it does not identify an otherwise unknown person as Abdullah.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The demonstratives share this construction: ذاك points to something distant, while أولئك and the other forms follow the same pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With هو and related pronouns, the accusative state should clarify or confirm the referent, as معروفا or بينا; an action like منطلقا does not identify him.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · ابن دارة | reports | Ibn Dāra's line illustrates the pronoun construction with معروفا as an identifying circumstantial state.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A demonstrative may also identify something present, as in هذا عبد الله فاعرفه, but here it serves recognition rather than marking a pronoun.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Pronouns can be followed by circumstantial descriptions in boasting or threatening contexts, when the speaker reminds the listener of known qualities such as generosity or bravery.
[SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهاتانوهؤلاءوذلكPageV02P077وذانك#232/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A pronoun normally assumes an already known referent, so a following name or action as mere new information is unsuitable; an unknown speaker behind a wall can identify himself, and an ordinary noun such as أخوك permits the construction.

item.text: The main disagreements so far concern the threat of *rajm*, what “leave me” requires, and whether *maliyyan* describes duration or safety. I’m also tracking the grammar and rhetorical notes separately.
